newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-KIDD QUITS AS IRELAND COACH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-KIDD QUITS AS IRELAND COACH.

text.p: Murray Kidd quit as Ireland coach following a lengthy meeting with the Irish Rugby Football Union on Tuesday.
"I am standing down with regret and I offer every best wishes to the team," said Kidd.
Bobby Deacy, the IRFU president, confirmed that he had accepted Kidd's resignation.
New Zealander Kidd had been summoned to the meeting following Ireland's surprise 39-37 home defeat by Italy on Saturday.
It was the latest in a poor run of results under Kidd who was appointed as the country's first full-time coach 15 months ago.
He has seen Ireland lose six of their last seven internationals.
But Kidd, who has spoken to some of the players about Ireland's troubled build-up to the Five Nations championship, insisted he had done all he could to motivate his struggling side.
"A few of the players have been in touch with me and feel our preparation (for the Italian game) was excellent," he said.
"The players felt maybe they let themselves down on the day. None of the players I spoke to blamed me for what has happened over the last few weeks."
Ireland, who finished bottom of last season's Five Nations championship, kick off this year's campaign with a daunting battle against France in Dublin in just under two weeks.
